lessons.title: Story Time: A Voyage Across the Ocean
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to discuss the setting of a story and how it affects events.
success_criteria: I can describe the setting.
I can say how the setting affects the story.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at ocean pictures and predict a story set there.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a story set on the ocean, modelling discussion of how the setting shapes events (storms, waves).
lessons.independent_task: Children describe the story's setting and discuss how it affected what happened.
key_questions: How did the setting cause a problem?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain setting's effect in full sentences

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of setting's role — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap the story's setting and key events.

lessons.title: Counting in 2s
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count in multiples of 2 to 20.
success_criteria: I can count in 2s to 20.
I can spot a pattern in counting in 2s.
lessons.starter_activity: Count fish/sea creature pairs (e.g. pairs of flippers).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting in 2s using ocean-themed objects (pairs of shells, fish), noting the even number pattern.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise counting in 2s using ocean-themed counters, recording the sequence.

differentiation.greater_depth: Count in 2s to 20 and beyond, spotting odd/even

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting in multiples skill — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Practise counting in 2s using pairs of shoes or socks.

lessons.title: The Five Oceans
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name the world's oceans on a map.
success_criteria: I can name at least 2 oceans.
I can point to an ocean on a world map.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a world map and spot the blue areas.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce the five oceans (Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic) using a world map.
lessons.independent_task: Children label the oceans on a simple world map outline.
key_questions: Can you find the Atlantic Ocean?

differentiation.greater_depth: Label all 5 oceans and name a bordering continent

lessons.assessment_notes: Note locational knowledge of oceans — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.home_link: Find the oceans on a map or globe at home if available.

lessons.title: Writing Ocean Adjectives and Sentences
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write descriptive sentences about the ocean.
success_criteria: I can use an adjective to describe the ocean.
I can write a full sentence.
lessons.starter_activity: Brainstorm ocean adjectives as a class.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a descriptive sentence about the ocean using adjectives.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 descriptive sentences about the ocean.
key_questions: What does the ocean look/sound like?
Can you write a sentence about it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive vocabulary and sentence construction — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share ocean sentences with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe the ocean to your family using new adjectives.

lessons.title: Counting in 5s and 10s
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count in multiples of 5 and 10 to 50.
success_criteria: I can count in 5s to 50.
I can count in 10s to 50.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model counting in 5s and 10s using ocean-themed objects grouped accordingly.
lessons.independent_task: Children practise counting in 5s and 10s, recording sequences.

differentiation.support: Count in 10s only to 50 with objects

lessons.assessment_notes: Record counting in multiples skill — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Practise counting in 5s or 10s using coins or toys.

lessons.title: Sea Creatures and Their Homes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name sea creatures and describe where they live in the ocean.
success_criteria: I can name 3 sea creatures.
I can say where in the ocean they live.
lessons.starter_activity: Guess sea creatures from picture clues.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss different ocean zones (surface, reef, deep sea) and creatures found in each.
lessons.independent_task: Children match sea creatures to their ocean zone, recording their matching.
resources_needed: Sea creature and ocean zone picture cards
lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of ocean habitats — evidence for GEOG.2/SCI links.
lessons.plenary: Recap ocean zones and their creatures.
lessons.home_link: Look up a sea creature and where it lives.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Ocean Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read ocean-themed words.
success_criteria: I can blend and read ocean words.
I can read a sentence about the ocean.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending ocean-themed words (e.g. 'wave', 'fish', 'deep').
lessons.independent_task: Children read ocean-themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading ocean words over the week.

lessons.title: Measuring Capacity: Full and Empty
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare capacity using ocean-themed containers.
success_criteria: I can say which container holds more.
I can use the words full, empty, half full.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss which of two containers looks like it holds more.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model filling containers with water/sand and comparing capacity, introducing full/empty/half full vocabulary.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare the capacity of different containers, recording which holds more.
key_questions: Is this container full or half full?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record capacity comparison skill — evidence for MATHS.MEA.
lessons.home_link: Compare the capacity of two containers at home (e.g. cups).

lessons.title: Ocean Pollution and Caring for the Sea
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way to help look after the ocean.
success_criteria: I can say why the ocean needs looking after.
I can name one way to help.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what might happen if litter goes into the sea.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss ocean pollution simply and sensitively, focusing on positive actions we can take.
lessons.independent_task: Children draw and describe one way to help look after the ocean (e.g. recycling, not littering).
key_questions: Why is it important to look after the ocean?
What can you do to help?

differentiation.greater_depth: Explain the impact of pollution on sea creatures

lessons.assessment_notes: Note environmental awareness — evidence for GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Recap ways to help protect the ocean.
lessons.home_link: Do one thing at home to help the environment, like recycling.

lessons.title: Writing a Postcard from the Ocean
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a simple postcard describing an imagined ocean adventure.
success_criteria: I can write 2-3 sentences about my ocean adventure.
I can use capital letters and full stops.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a postcard describing an imagined ocean adventure.
lessons.independent_task: Children write their own ocean adventure postcard.
key_questions: What did you see on your ocean adventure?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note imaginative writing and punctuation use — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share ocean postcards with the class.
lessons.home_link: Read your postcard to your family.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting in Multiples and Capacity
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting in multiples and capacity comparison skills.
success_criteria: I can count in 2s, 5s and 10s.
I can compare capacity.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of counting in 2s/5s/10s and capacity comparison.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: counting in multiples, capacity comparison.
key_questions: What comes next in this count?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 16 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/MEA.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising counting in multiples over the weekend.

lessons.title: Where in the World? Locating Famous Seas
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to locate a named sea on a simple map.
success_criteria: I can find a named sea on a map.
I can say which continent it's near.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the five oceans from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce a couple of named seas (e.g. Mediterranean Sea, Red Sea) and their locations.
lessons.independent_task: Children locate and label named seas on a simple map, noting nearby continents.

differentiation.greater_depth: Locate 3+ seas and name bordering countries/continents

lessons.assessment_notes: Note extended locational knowledge — evidence for GEOG.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap seas located on the map.
lessons.home_link: Find a sea or ocean on a map or globe together.

lessons.title: Ocean Facts Show and Tell
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to share an ocean fact learned this week clearly.
success_criteria: I can share one ocean fact.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear, interesting fact to share.
lessons.independent_task: Children share their favourite ocean fact from the week with a small group, answering a question.
resources_needed: Work from the week for reference
key_questions: What is your favourite ocean fact?
Can you answer a question about it?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and factual recall progress — evidence for ENG.SL1/GEOG.1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all the ocean facts shared.
lessons.home_link: Share your favourite ocean fact with your family.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Full Week Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply all maths skills learned this week in a mixed challenge.
success_criteria: I can count in multiples.
I can compare capacity.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the week's key maths vocabulary.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's full maths content.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a mixed review worksheet covering counting in multiples and capacity.

differentiation.support: Complete with reduced complexity and support

lessons.assessment_notes: Final week 16 maths assessment summary for each child.
lessons.home_link: Review the week's maths learning together.

lessons.title: Oceans Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key facts about the world's oceans learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name the oceans.
I can name a sea creature and its habitat.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the week's learning about oceans.
lessons.independent_task: Contribute to a class 'Oceans of the World' display combining maps, creature matching, and postcards from the week.
key_questions: What have we learned about oceans this week?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note synthesis of the week's learning — evidence for GEOG.1/GEOG.2.
lessons.plenary: Unveil the finished 'Oceans of the World' display.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about oceans with your family.
